title: Collaborative Language Agents | EECS at UC Berkeley
content: Collaborative Language Agents | EECS at UC Berkeley Collaborative Language Agents Jessy Lin EECS Department, University of California, Berkeley Technical Report No. UCB/EECS-2026-2 January 6, 2026 http://www2.eecs.berkeley.edu/Pubs/TechRpts/2026/EECS-2026-2.pdf Large language models have achieved remarkable performance on standardized benchmarks. However, real-world applications demand more than answering questions or executing actions within fully-defined environmentsâthey require models capable of interacting with humans who bring their own context, goals, and preferences. This thesis addresses a central question: how do we design models that can effectively collaborate with humans? I approach this challenge through three complementary perspectives: evaluation, architecture, and learning objectives. First, I introduce DialOp, a benchmark for assessing how language model agents and humans make complex everyday decisions together, providing a rigorous framework for measuring collaborative capabilities. Second, I demonstrate how augmenting language model architectures with memory layers enables efficient knowledge updates, establishing a foundation for continual learning across interactions. Third, I extend these ideas beyond text to embodied, multimodal agents, showing how unifying language learning with world modeling objectives enables agents to understand diverse forms of human communication, including feedback. Together, these contributions advance the development of AI systems that can collaborate with humans not only in digital environments but eventually in the physical world.
